title: The tooth fights back: pulp to periapex
topic: The lines of immune defense from dentin to the periapex, and why the lesion contains but cannot reach the canal infection.

claims.claim: Odontoblasts sense bacteria: TLR2, TLR4 (receptors localized in human odontoblasts and their processes)
claims.source: Veerayutthwilai et al., Oral Microbiol Immunol 2007;22:5-13 (PMID 17241164)

claims.claim: Dendritic cells sample; then T cells, macrophages, neutrophils (accumulate as caries deepens)
claims.source: Farges et al., Mediators Inflamm 2015;2015:230251 (PMID 26538821), review

claims.claim: Necrotic pulp: no immune access, a protected bacterial reservoir
claims.source: Graves et al., J Oral Microbiol 2011;3:5304 (PMID 21547019), review

claims.claim: Periapical lesion cells: macrophages, T + B cells, plasma cells (neutrophils and antibodies drawn; unranked)
claims.source: Stashenko et al., J Endod 1992;18:422-6 (PMID 9796508), abstract: cell composition of human or rat lesions

claims.claim: Plasma cells in periapical granulomas make mostly IgG (81.9% of immunoglobulin-positive plasma cells, 10 human granulomas)
claims.source: Matthews & Mason, Br J Oral Surg 1983;21:192-7 (PMID 6578841)

claims.claim: IL-1, TNF, PGE2, RANKL switch on osteoclasts; osteoclasts resorb bone (signals shown side by side; review-level model)
claims.source: Graves et al., J Oral Microbiol 2011;3:5304 (PMID 21547019), review; Wang & Stashenko, J Endod 1993;19:107-11 (PMID 8509747)

claims.claim: The lesion contains the infection but cannot reach the canal; treatment can (it reduces the canal's microbial load)
claims.source: Márton & Kiss, Oral Microbiol Immunol 2000;15:139-50 (PMID 11154396), review; Graves et al., J Oral Microbiol 2011;3:5304 (PMID 21547019), review; Nair, Crit Rev Oral Biol Med 2004;15:348-81 (PMID 15574679), review

claims.claim: Schematic: 'human + rodent data' - cells and mediators from human tissue studies; sequence and kinetics largely from rodent models; cell numbers, sizes and timing illustrative
claims.source: Stashenko et al., J Endod 1992;18:422-6 (PMID 9796508); Graves et al. 2011 (PMID 21547019)

caption:
The tooth fights back: dentin to apex.

Odontoblasts carry TLR2/TLR4. Dendritic cells sample; T cells, macrophages, neutrophils follow as caries deepens.
A necrotic canal: out of immune reach.
The lesion usually contains the infection (plasma cells: mostly IgG). The cost is bone: IL-1, TNF, PGE2, RANKL (review model).
It can't reach the canal. Treatment can.

Schematic animation; human + rodent data.
Refs: Veerayutthwilai 2007, Oral Microbiol Immunol; Farges 2015, Mediators Inflamm; Graves 2011, J Oral Microbiol; Márton & Kiss 2000, Oral Microbiol Immunol; Matthews & Mason 1983, Br J Oral Surg; Nair 2004, Crit Rev Oral Biol Med
